IC1: 1. Had a diagnosis of PHN [OR], DN [OR], CRPS [OR], carpal tunnel syndrome [OR], HIV neuropathy [OR], idiopathic sensory neuropathy [OR], or other peripheral neuropathy (upon mutual agreement of the sponsor and investigator)
IC2: 2. Patients with PHN [AND] must have had pain >3 months after rash healing
IC3: 3. Patients with DN must have had Type I or II diabetes and painful distal symmetric sensorimotor polyneuropathy with or without dynamic allodynia of the lower extremities
IC4: 4. Patients with CRPS must have met current IASP (International Association for the Study of Pain) diagnostic criteria
IC5: 5. Patients with carpal tunnel syndrome [AND] must have had a diagnosis by combination clinical neurological examination (e.g., Phalen's and Tinel's signs), electrodiagnostic testing, and daily painful symptoms of at least 3 months' duration
IC6: 6. Patients with HIV neuropathy must have had HIV, subjective symptoms of painful peripheral neuropathy, and daily painful symptoms of at least 3 months' duration
IC7: 7. Patients with idiopathic sensory neuropathy [AND] must have had pain of at least 3 months' duration
IC8: 8. Reached an average daily pain rating [AND] during the baseline week of pain ratings greater than 4 on the 0-to-10 numerical pain rating scale (Question 5 of the BPI)
IC9: 9. Had never received an analgesic regimen that contained lidocaine [OR] or gabapentin
